audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Rumble 6 of 7 stages while Warwick wins the matchup 53.36%.
audit.why: Rumble's edge is real only while Flamespitter out-ranges a melee walk-up (levels 1-3). Once Warwick has Infinite Duress (1.5s suppression, point-and-click, 110s at rank 1) plus Blade of the Ruined King, a single connect removes Rumble from the fight, and Rumble's Overheat lockout gives a free window every rotation.
audit.corrected: Rumble L1, Skill L2, Rumble L3, Skill L4-5, Warwick L6 / first item / 2+ items, with ratings raised to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game spike text treats Rumble's burn scaling as decisive and never states Warwick's own spikes.
audit.why: Warwick spikes at 6 (suppression) and at Blade of the Ruined King (%HP + sustain engine); Rumble's Overheat is a hard spell lockout that is Warwick's cleanest engage window all game.
audit.corrected: Spike text now names the Overheat lockout as the engage window and Rumble's 80s rank-3 Equalizer cooldown as the thing that cannot answer it.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text labels Scrap Shield as (E) and Electro Harpoon as (E); The Equalizer is described as something Infinite Duress 'can't cross'.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is W, Electro Harpoon is E. The Equalizer is a damaging, slowing flame wall in Riot's text — it is not pathing terrain, so it does not stop a leap. Warwick's E Primal Howl gives 2.5s of damage reduction before the 1s flee, which is the correct answer to a Danger-Zone Flamespitter cone.
audit.corrected: Slots relabelled W/E; Equalizer described as damage+slow that Infinite Duress can cross; Primal Howl's 2.5s damage reduction tied to the Flamespitter cone; Scrap Shield's 6s cooldown used as the trade gate.

audit.why: Scrap Shield at a flat 6s is the punishable window and the page already keys trades to it; now stated with the number.

edits.before: His Scrap Shield and heat-managed Q keep beating your trades through 4-5.
edits.after: Trade when Scrap Shield (W) is down — its 6s cooldown gates the 4-5 window.

edits.before: The Equalizer zones your engage path the moment he hits 6.
edits.after: Infinite Duress suppresses him at 6 through any heat window.

edits.before: Liandry's percent-burn on his Q out-sustains you after his first item.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King plus your passive out-sustains his burn.

edits.before: Overheat-managed Flamespitter and Equalizer keep Rumble ahead all game.
edits.after: His Overheat window is your free R engage — one suppress ends him.

edits.before: In the Danger Zone Rumble's Flamespitter (Q) melts you while Scrap Shield (E) and the Electro Harpoon (E) slow keep you at range — his heat-boosted rotation out-DPSes your all-in.
edits.after: In the Danger Zone Flamespitter (Q) melts you while Scrap Shield (W) and the Electro Harpoon (E) slow keep you at range — his heat-boosted rotation out-DPSes your level-3 all-in.

edits.before: The Equalizer (R) zones your entire engage path; he drops it between you and him and your Infinite Duress can't cross it safely.
edits.after: The Equalizer (R) carpets your path in damage and slow, but it is not terrain — Infinite Duress crosses it; leap once it burns out.

edits.before: Rumble's overheated Flamespitter plus Equalizer keep him ahead — only threaten him when his heat is redlined and Q/shield are down.
edits.after: Overheating locks him out of every spell for its duration — that silence window is your free R engage, and his 80s R cannot answer it.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are all Rumble: boosted Flamespitter (Q) melts you, Scrap Shield (E) and the Harpoon slow kite your dashes, and heat management lets him win any extended trade against your sustain. Farm from range.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 hinge on Scrap Shield (W, 6s): when it is down, Q-bite in and hold Primal Howl (E) for his Danger-Zone Flamespitter — 2.5s of damage reduction eats the cone. While W is up, farm and give him nothing.

edits.before: Liandry's-boosted burn plus The Equalizer (R) zoning keep him ahead through items. Engage only when he's Overheated and silenced, and lean on jungle pressure to break the lane.
edits.after: His burn items scale, but Infinite Duress is a point-and-click 1.5s suppress that removes him from the fight outright. Engage on his Overheat lockout, and keep Grievous Wounds up for his shielding.

notes: Rumble's kit file flags Scrap Shield (W) with 'knockup' and 'terrain'; Riot's description is only a shield plus a burst of move speed, so both are tooltip-parsing misfires and I asserted neither. The Equalizer's 'terrain' flag is likewise a misfire — Riot's text is a damaging, slowing flame wall, so I did not claim it blocks Infinite Duress. Packet suspectName whys[3] 'His Scrap Shield' is a FALSE POSITIVE (correct Riot name); the real naming error was spikes[0].text labelling Scrap Shield as (E). Chart flipped to match the 53.36% win rate; if the mirror rumble__warwick still holds Rumble at 6/7, mirror-fix will need this side treated as authoritative because the packet defect flags the contradiction on both.
